The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. The portraits, the books chosen, and their interpretation offer unique insights into the diverse lives an Using a mix of moving image and photography, the artwork builds a sensory and emotive portrait of women in midlife. Covering themes of menopause, mental health, climate change, and marital breakdown, this work explores the ways women have reclaimed the word witch and sought solac Speaking about the exhibition , Rosie Reed Hillman says: “I have worked to build rapport with contributors over the last four years and believe the intimate access conveyed in this project creates an exhibition that inspires empathy, curiosity and a greater understanding of issue “Women in midlife of all backgrounds are an overlooked demographic who want to see art and hear stories that reflect their experiences, and I hope this work speaks to them especially.”

The free concert is a unique opportunity to shape future research on hearing aids while enjoying live music Trevor Cox, Professor of acoustic engineering at the University of Salford, explains: “We don’t think anything like this has been attempted before. Music is an afterthou “But music is such an important part of our lives, it brings us together for shared experiences that people with hearing issues can feel locked out of. Having ended her marriage the year she turned 40 and begun questioning the life she once imagined for hersel A former features editor at a glossy fashion magazine, she finds work at a local newspaper – and is promptly tasked with interviewing a series of distressingly inspiring women who appear to be effortlessly balancing successful careers with motherhood. Initially, these encounters Inspired by Kerr’s own experiences, Spent Hen gradually moves from isolation towards tentative optimism, as its protagonist begins speaking openly about miscarriage, infertility and childlessness, finding that the stories she has kept to herself resonate far more widely than she As Kerr questions the images of perfect families that can alienate those who cannot or do not have children, the play grows into a candid, wry exploration of grief and identity, while thoughtfully confronting the social pressure to conform to a rigid conception of a fulfilled lif Spent Hen runs at 53two from Wed 21 to Fri 23 October, before heading to Audenshaw’s Guide Bridge Theatre on Wed 28 Oct

raw_evidence: Manchester Airport station is set for a major £115m upgrade from December, with Network Rail and contractor Kier preparing to begin a programme designed to increase capacity and improve journeys for millions of passengers The works will see Platforms 1, 2 and 3 extended to accommodate longer trains, alongside upgrades to the track layout approaching the station and a modernised signalling system The programme is expected to run through to 2028, with the improvements intended to allow more trains to operate while making journeys to and from the airport more reliable The first major stage will take place on Sun 6 Dec, when Manchester Airport station will close for one day while engineers begin the works. Rail replacement buses will operate between Wilmslow and Manchester Airport, while Metrolink services will continue to run as normal The investment forms part of the wider Manchester Rail Upgrade programme, which aims to create a bigger and better-connected railway across Greater Manchester and the North West. Once complete, the station improvements will support future passenger growth and strengthen the airpo Rail minister Lord Hendy said: “ Manchester Airport is a vital transport hub and this £115m investment from government will deliver more reliable services, increase capacity, and improve connections for the millions of passengers who use the station every year

Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. Tickets . . . . . . . Ruby Turner is widely recognised as one of the UK’s leading soul singers, known for her powerful performances across soul, R&B, and reggae. She has earned praise not only for her solo albums and live shows but also for her frequent collaborations with Jools Holland’s Rhythm & Blues Orchestra. . . Ruby Turner began a successful run as a solo artist in the late 1980s, landing a chart-topping hit with "It's Gonna Be Alright," and releasing numerous respected albums and singles over the coming years that traversed soul, gospel, and pop. She became a frequent collaborator with Jools Holland and performed with an array of high-profile stars from Mick Jagger to Steve Winwood. . . Her debut album, Woman Hold Up Half the Sky (1986), was a critical and commercial success, and she went on to release another 13 albums over the course of the next three decades, including 1989's Paradise, which peaked at number 39 on the Billboard R&B chart. She also charted eight singles throughout the 80s and 90s, the most successful of which was "I'd Rather Go Blind". . . On 4 June 2012 Ruby performed 'You Are So Beautiful' with Jools Holland at the Queen's Diamond Jubilee Concert outside Buckingham Palace in London. In autumn 2012, Ruby was a guest judge on the BBC's The Choir: Sing While You Work with choirmaster Gareth Malone and in 2013 Ruby was a guest judge on the BBC's Songs of Praise Gospel Choirs competition. raw_evidence: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. raw_evidence: A moonlit community run which aims to empower women and girls to stay active and enjoy outdoor exercise through the winter months comes to Platt Fields Park this week Organised by Manchester Parks in partnership with the running community, the welcoming and inclusive event is not just for experienced runners but for people just getting started and who are looking to become more active, helping them connect with local walking or running groups The event offers a chance to meet local run clubs, find new running partners and pick up tips to run safely through the darker months. Taking place on Thu 22 Oct from 6pm-9pm, the event is open to all genders and abilities, but organisers hope that it will be particularly helpful The first event earlier this year saw 210 people take part to complete a 3k run or walk around the park in a series of waves. Some of the more experienced runners even completed all seven waves and bagged themselves a half marathon The format will be similar this month, with guided runs led by local clubs with several running/jogging waves of a 3k route around the park. Free head torches will be available on a first-come, first-served basis. Attendees are also encouraged to wear lights and fluorescent cloth A small event village will have stalls with representatives from fitness groups, community safety organisations, and charities, and there will be food and drink vendors and music
